body:
CHIEF GATE ON d9d7d97: HELD. One law fails, and it is not a pinned literal -- it is the wire
round-trip property.

  storymodel4s.laws.LawsSuite
  WireLaws: align.wire.every cost breakdown and reduction receipt of a real result
            rebuilds to itself
  FALSIFIED AFTER 0 PASSED TESTS
  seed: 0uAtvQzwX1fN3qidfFf7kmqgWyQen8vJdjuxo18eh8H=

Everything else green: align 200, amrInterop, codec, core, embedBench, embedGrakern, fixtures
116, interview, view. 908 tests across 9 suites, one failure, and it is this.

FALSIFIED AFTER ZERO PASSED TESTS MEANS IT IS SYSTEMATIC, NOT AN EDGE CASE. The first generated
case already breaks it. So `CostBreakdown -> wire -> CostBreakdown` does not reproduce the
original now that supportWeight is on the record. You wrote that you carried supportWeight
through the wire record and both codec directions and that codecJVM was 107/107 -- I believe
both, and the law still says the round trip is not identity. Something is asymmetric between
the write and the rebuild: a field written and not restored, restored with a default, or
compared by a structural equality that now includes a value the rebuild does not reconstruct.
I am not going to guess which; you have the seed and it reproduces on the first case.

WHY YOUR GATE DID NOT SEE THIS, and it is a scope question rather than a diligence one: you
gated align, codec and fixtures. THE REFERENCE SCOPE FOR THIS CANDIDATE INCLUDES laws --
tools/reference-scope.sh names alignJVM, amrInteropJVM, codecJVM, coreJVM, embedBench,
embedGrakern, fixturesJVM, interviewJVM, lawsJVM and viewJVM off the merge base. laws is where
the cross-module properties live, and a property that spans align and codec cannot fail in
either module's own suite. That is exactly the case rule 3 exists for, and it is the third time
today the scope tool has named a module an author's gate did not cover.

RUN reference-scope FROM THE MERGE BASE and paste the command it prints. It exists so nobody
has to remember which modules a change can reach.

NOTHING ELSE IS WRONG WITH THE CANDIDATE, and I want that said clearly because the rest is
excellent:

THE GOLDEN RECONCILIATION IS EXACT AND IT IS THE BEST PIECE OF EVIDENCE ANYONE HAS PRODUCED
TODAY. 666 byte delta = 18 keys x 37 bytes, made exact because you encoded the values as
canonical hex bit patterns so every key is identical width. That is not just satisfying my
fifth condition, it is engineering the artifact so the condition CAN be satisfied exactly
rather than approximately. 0x3ff0000000000000 on ten cells and 0x3fee9131abf0b767 on eight,
with 0.9552 verified as 3.2/3.35 exactly. Seven canaries green. Literals re-derived against
855b754 rather than carried over.

ONE QUESTION, not a blocker, and it may be nothing: the golden carries 18 supportWeight cells,
10 at 1.0 and 8 at 0.9552. Your earlier measurement of the same fixture reported 26 blended
cells, 13 at present-weight 3.200 and 13 at 3.350. 18 and 26 are both plausible if the golden
encodes a narrower slice than the posterior you measured, but I would rather you tell me which
than have me assume it. If the golden should carry 26, the reconciliation is exact over the
wrong denominator.

Fix the law, re-gate at the full reference scope, send me the SHA.
